How to use this calculator

  2. Select Calculate to see the answer and its breakdown.
  3. Keep a scenario, change an input and compare the results.

Use consistent units and check the assumptions below before applying the result.

How bandwidth is calculated

Estimate transfer time or required data rate from file size and network speed, with decimal or binary byte units and an efficiency allowance. The ideal rate ignores latency, congestion, protocol overhead, server limits, and competing traffic; real transfers often take longer. A 1 GB decimal file over 100 Mbps takes about 80 seconds at full theoretical speed. The calculation validates each input and keeps its stated units explicit. Real links spend capacity on protocol overhead and other traffic. This is an estimate for the stated assumptions; confirm measurements and any applicable professional or local standards before relying on it.

seconds = file bits ÷ effective bits per second
A worked example

A 1 GB decimal file over 100 Mbps takes about 80 seconds at full theoretical speed.

Assumptions & useful context

The result depends on the values you enter and the method described above. Displayed numbers may be rounded; calculations use the unrounded values. Check that this model matches your situation before relying on it.

Frequently asked questions

Why is there an efficiency setting?

Real links spend capacity on protocol overhead and other traffic.

Are Mbps and MB/s the same?

No. One byte contains eight bits, so 80 Mbps equals 10 MB/s before overhead.
